mainTopic: The third wall of a סוכה (corner and מבוי shapes, צורת הפתח) and whether a סוכה wall counts for שבת (מגו)
overview: The גמרא continues discussing a סוכה with two full walls and a third wall of only one טפח. רב's ruling that the טפח is placed 'כנגד היוצא' is supported by שמואל in the name of לוי and by the ruling of the בית מדרש. רבי סימון (or רבי יהושע בן לוי) offers another method: a slightly wide טפח placed less than three טפחים from a wall, so that through לבוד it counts as a bigger wall. For a סוכה shaped like an alleyway (two parallel walls), רב יהודה allows a single טפח on any side, but רבי סימון requires a board of four טפחים and a bit. The גמרא explains the difference: walls that meet at a corner are a real structure, while parallel walls are not. רבא is quoted in three versions about using a צורת הפתח, and רב כהנא follows the version that requires both the טפח and the צורת הפתח. רבא then rules by מגו that a valid סוכה wall also counts as a wall for שבת during סוכות. אביי challenges this from a ברייתא, and רבא defends it by rereading the ברייתא and by a כל שכן argument. The amud ends by starting a fresh look at רבא's ruling about סכך over a מבוי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Students suggest a diagonal placement and רב stays silent
steps.stepSummary: רב's students ask why the טפח should not be placed diagonally across the open corner ('כנגד ראש תור'), and רב does not answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב:] But let him place it opposite the 'ראש תור' (diagonally)! רב was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב's students challenge his ruling about where the one-טפח wall goes. They suggest a diagonal placement that would seem to close off the סוכה better, and רב does not respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had said the טפח is placed at the end of one wall, facing the other wall ('כנגד היוצא'). The students argue that slanting it diagonally, like the narrowing edge of a plowed furrow, would make the shape look more closed, almost like a triangle. רב himself does not answer, but steps 2 and 3 show that רב's view has strong support.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him place it (a suggestion that works as a challenge)
Opposite, facing
The end of a furrow line, meaning a diagonal, slanting placement
Was silent

steps.confusionAlert: רב's silence does not mean he gave up his position. The very next line ('איתמר נמי') brings support for exactly what רב said.

phrases.english: But let him place it opposite the end of the furrow line (diagonally)!
phrases.notes: The speakers (רב כהנא and רב אסי) were introduced on the previous amud.

phrases.english: Rav was silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling (earlier) that the טפח is placed כנגד היוצא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's placement of the טפח 'כנגד היוצא'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A diagonal placement seems to close the open corner better and look more like a real enclosure, so why not require or allow that?

steps.title: שמואל quoting לוי agrees with רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a parallel statement: שמואל in the name of לוי also says the טפח is placed כנגד היוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: שמואל said in the name of לוי: He places it opposite the wall that goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב by quoting another authority, שמואל in the name of לוי, who says exactly the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'איתמר נמי' tells us this is an independent tradition that matches רב. Even though רב himself did not answer his students, his ruling is confirmed by a second chain of teachers. 'כנגד היוצא' means the טפח stands at the end of one wall, facing the wall that extends out from the other end.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introduces support from another tradition)
In the name of
The one that goes out, meaning the wall that extends outward

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Shmuel said in the name of Levi:
He places it opposite the wall that goes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּלֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב after his silence in response to the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that the טפח is placed כנגד היוצא
steps.raayaSupportSource: An independent tradition from שמואל in the name of לוי

steps.title: The study hall rules the same way
steps.stepSummary: The practical ruling taught in the בית מדרש is also that the טפח is placed כנגד היוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too they rule in the study hall: He places it opposite the wall that goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that this was the actual practical ruling taught in the בית מדרש. This settles רב's method as the accepted practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מורין' means giving a practical halachic ruling, not just theory. So beyond one supporting opinion, this placement was the standard instruction people were given. The diagonal suggestion of the students is therefore not the accepted practice.

keyTerms.meaning: And so they rule (a practical halachic instruction)
The study hall, the בית מדרש

steps.whatToRemember: Final practical ruling for a corner-shaped סוכה: the one-טפח third wall is placed at the end of one wall, facing the other wall (כנגד היוצא), not diagonally.

phrases.english: And similarly, they rule in the study hall:
He places it opposite the wall that goes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the practical ruling of the בית מדרש on top of the support from שמואל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical ruling follows רב: the טפח is placed כנגד היוצא.

steps.title: A wider handbreadth placed near the wall, joined by לבוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימון (or רבי יהושע בן לוי) says to make a slightly wide טפח and place it less than three טפחים from a wall, since anything that close counts as joined (לבוד).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי סימון, and some say רבי יהושע בן לוי, said: He makes for it a generous טפח, and places it less than three טפחים next to the wall, and anything less than three next to the wall is considered joined (לבוד).
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives another way to set up the third wall. He uses the rule of לבוד so that the small טפח, plus the gap, counts as a bigger wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed (לבוד). So a gap of almost three, plus a slightly wide טפח (טפח שוחק), adds up to a wall of more than four טפחים. That is more than half of a seven-טפחים wall, so it now looks like a real wall and not just a small marker.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (the statement is attributed to a different sage)
A 'laughing' handbreadth, measured with fingers spread, slightly larger than a regular טפח
Next to the wall
Joined, the rule that a gap under three טפחים is treated as closed

steps.confusionAlert: The טפח is not touching the wall. It stands just under three טפחים away, and לבוד treats that gap as if it were filled in.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key tool in הלכות סוכה: using לבוד to turn a small piece into a wall of meaningful size (four טפחים, more than half of seven).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי סִימוֹן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Simon, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, said:
He makes for it a generous (slightly wide) handbreadth,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַעֲמִידוֹ בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים סָמוּךְ לַדּוֹפֶן,
phrases.english: and places it less than three handbreadths away, next to the wall,
and anything less than three handbreadths next to the wall
is considered as if joined (lavud).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי סִימוֹן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different method for the third wall than רב's 'כנגד היוצא'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Make a טפח שוחק and place it less than three טפחים from the wall, so by לבוד it counts as a wall of more than four טפחים.

steps.title: A sukkah shaped like an alleyway is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a סוכה with two parallel walls, like a מבוי, is כשרה, and the third טפח may be placed on any open side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: A סוכה made like an alleyway is כשרה, and that טפח, he places it on any side he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה moves to a new shape of סוכה: two walls facing each other, open at both ends like a מבוי. He rules it is כשרה and gives freedom where to put the טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the case was two walls meeting at a corner. Here the two full walls are parallel, leaving two open ends. רב יהודה says this shape is still כשרה with just the one-טפח third wall, and that טפח can go at either open end, next to either wall.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway, open at both ends with two parallel walls
Kosher, valid
Side, direction

steps.whatToRemember: Two shapes of סוכה with 'two and a טפח': a corner shape (טפח placed כנגד היוצא, or by רבי סימון's לבוד method), and an alleyway shape (כשרה according to רב יהודה, with the טפח on any side; the next step brings a stricter view).

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A sukkah made like an alleyway is fit,
and that handbreadth, he places it
on any side that he wishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: סוּכָּה הָעֲשׂוּיָה כְּמָבוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from a corner-shaped סוכה to a סוכה with two parallel walls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה shaped like a מבוי is כשרה, and the third טפח may be placed on whichever side he chooses.

steps.title: A parallel-walled סוכה needs a board of four טפחים and a bit
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימון (or רבי יהושע בן לוי) says that a סוכה with two parallel walls needs a board slightly wider than four טפחים. It is placed less than three טפחים from one of the walls, and the gap counts as closed because of לבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי סימון, and some say רבי יהושע בן לוי, said: He makes a board four טפחים and a little bit wide. He stands it less than three טפחים from the wall. Anything less than three טפחים from the wall is treated as if it were attached.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the same אמורא gives his ruling for the מבוי-shaped סוכה from step 5. He disagrees with רב יהודה: a small טפח is not enough, and you need a board a bit wider than four טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The board is a bit over four טפחים wide. The gap between it and the wall is under three טפחים, and לבוד treats that gap as closed. Together they make a wall about seven טפחים wide, which is the minimum width of a סוכה. So one open side becomes a full, real wall.

keyTerms.meaning: A board or plank used as a partial wall
Four טפחים and a little bit more
And he stands it up (sets it in place)
Near the wall

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 4. There, for the corner-shaped סוכה, a small טפח was enough. Here, for the parallel-walled סוכה, you need a board of four טפחים and a bit. It is the same speaker, but he is talking about a different case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Simon, and some say
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, said:
He makes for it a board of four handbreadths and a bit,
and stands it less than three handbreadths from the wall,
phrases.notes: Placed on one of the open ends, near one of the parallel walls.

phrases.english: and anything less than three handbreadths near the wall
is considered joined (לבוד).
phrases.notes: Board (4+) plus the closed gap (under 3) gives a 7-טפח wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי סִימוֹן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה in step 5 about the מבוי-shaped סוכה: a single טפח is not enough, so a board of four טפחים and a bit is required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מבוי-shaped סוכה needs a board of four טפחים and a bit, placed less than three טפחים from a wall, so that it forms a seven-טפח wall through לבוד.

steps.title: Why does one case need a small טפח and the other a four-טפח board?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the corner-shaped סוכה only needs a טפח שוחק, while the parallel-walled סוכה needs a board of four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different there, where you said a slightly wide טפח is enough? And what is different here, where you said a four-טפח board is needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the two rulings of the same אמורא side by side and asks what makes them different. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the סוכה has two full walls and needs a third. So why the different size? The question is not attacking either ruling. It wants the reason for the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is different (asks for the reason behind a distinction)
There / here (the earlier case versus this case)
A slightly wide ("smiling") טפח, a bit more than one handbreadth
It is enough

phrases.english: And what is different there
where you say an expansive handbreadth is enough,
phrases.notes: The corner (L-shaped) סוכה from step 4.

phrases.english: and what is different here
where you say it requires a board of four?
phrases.notes: The parallel-walled (מבוי) סוכה from step 6.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם דְּקָאָמְרַתְּ סַגִּיא טֶפַח שׂוֹחֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the ruling in step 6 with the earlier ruling in step 4 and asks why they differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the corner-shaped סוכה needs only a טפח שוחק while the מבוי-shaped סוכה needs a four-טפח board.

steps.title: Joined walls need less help than walls that are not joined
steps.stepSummary: In the corner case, the two walls are joined properly, so a small טפח is enough. In the parallel case, the walls are not joined, so only a four-טפח board works.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, where there are two proper walls, a slightly wide טפח is enough. Here, where there are not two proper walls, if there is a four-טפח board, yes, it works. If not, no, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: it depends on how strong the two existing walls are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two walls meeting at a corner already make a real structure, so a small טפח is enough to finish it. Two parallel walls do not meet, so they are not "two walls" in the normal sense. That weaker setup needs a real, wide board to complete it.

keyTerms.meaning: In their proper, standard form (here: joined at a corner)
Where there is not

keyTerms.term: אִי אִיכָּא... אֵין, אִי לָא... לָא
keyTerms.meaning: If there is, yes; if not, no

steps.whatToRemember: Corner-shaped סוכה (walls joined): a טפח שוחק is enough. Parallel-walled סוכה (walls not joined): you need a board of four טפחים and a bit, placed within three טפחים of a wall.

phrases.english: There, where there are two walls in the proper way —
phrases.notes: The two walls meet at a corner.

phrases.english: an expansive handbreadth is enough for it,
here, where there are not two walls (in the proper way),
phrases.notes: Parallel walls do not meet.

phrases.english: if there is a board of four — yes,
if not — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two joined walls are a proper structure and need only a טפח to finish them. Parallel walls are not joined, so they need a four-טפח board.

steps.title: רבא: the corner-shaped סוכה also needs a doorway-frame
steps.stepSummary: In the first version of his words, רבא says the corner-shaped סוכה is kosher only through a צורת הפתח (doorway-frame). The טפח method alone does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And it is permitted only with a צורת הפתח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with the טפח method for the corner-shaped סוכה. In this version, the סוכה becomes kosher only by making a צורת הפתח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צורת הפתח is two upright posts with a crossbar on top. Halachically it counts as a partition, like a doorway. According to this version, the טפח שוחק of רבי סימון (or רבי יהושע בן לוי) is not enough by itself. The third side must be closed with a doorway-shape, for example by splitting the טפח into two posts and laying a beam across them.

keyTerms.meaning: The "form of a doorway": two posts with a beam across the top, which counts as a partition
It is permitted (kosher)
And it is not... except (only if)

phrases.english: Rava said: And it is not permitted
except with the form of a doorway.
phrases.notes: Refers to the corner-shaped סוכה with the טפח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְאֵינָהּ נִתֶּרֶת אֶלָּא בְּצוּרַת הַפֶּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the corner-shaped סוכה of step 4 and adds a stricter requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טפח שוחק method does not work by itself; the corner-shaped סוכה is kosher only through a צורת הפתח.

steps.title: Second version of רבא: a doorway-frame also works
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רבא was more lenient: a צורת הפתח is an additional way to make the סוכה kosher, not an extra requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא said: And it is also permitted with a צורת הפתח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different report of רבא's words. In this version he offers another option instead of adding a requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, "only" (אלא) makes the צורת הפתח the one valid method, so the טפח alone does not work. In this version, "also" (נמי) means the טפח works by itself, and a צורת הפתח is another valid way to complete the third wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (introduces a second version of a teaching)
Also

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions differ by a single word. "אֵינָהּ נִתֶּרֶת אֶלָּא" (only) makes the צורת הפתח required. "נִתֶּרֶת נָמֵי" (also) makes it just one more option. Read each word carefully.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two versions give different practical results. In the first, the טפח alone is not enough. In the second, the טפח alone works, and a צורת הפתח is another way.

phrases.english: Some say, Rava said:
And it is also permitted with the form of a doorway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָבָא: וְנִתֶּרֶת נָמֵי בְּצוּרַת הַפֶּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבא's statement from step 9, turning the requirement into an extra option.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צורת הפתח is another valid way to make the סוכה kosher; the טפח approach is not rejected.

steps.title: A version of רבא that requires both the טפח and the doorway-frame
steps.stepSummary: In another version (איכא דאמרי), רבא says the corner-shaped סוכה needs a צורת הפתח in addition to the טפח שוחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבא said: And it also needs a doorway-frame.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way that רבא's statement was reported. In this version, the טפח alone is not enough, and the צורת הפתח is an added requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a third version. Step 9 said only a צורת הפתח works. Step 10 said a צורת הפתח is just another option alongside the טפח. Here the word נמי ('also') means you need the טפח AND the צורת הפתח together. The next steps show that אמוראים really followed different versions in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces another version of a statement
It requires / it needs
Also / too

steps.confusionAlert: In the lenient version the word נמי means 'the צורת הפתח is ALSO a valid option.' In this version נמי means 'you ALSO need it, on top of the טפח.' The same word does opposite jobs in the two versions.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rava said:
And it also requires the form of a doorway.
phrases.notes: Added requirement on top of the טפח שוחק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter version of רבא, opposite to the lenient version in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The corner-shaped סוכה needs both a טפח שוחק and a צורת הפתח.

steps.title: רב אשי questions why רב כהנא makes both
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי sees רב כהנא making both a טפח שוחק and a צורת הפתח. He asks why, since one version of רבא says a צורת הפתח alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי found רב כהנא making an expansive טפח and also making a doorway-frame. He said to him: Doesn't the master hold like רבא, who said that the סוכה is also kosher with just a doorway-frame?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real-life practice. רב אשי challenges רב כהנא's practice of doing both, which seems like unnecessary extra work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי relies on the lenient version of רבא from step 10, where the צורת הפתח alone makes the סוכה kosher. Under that version, building the טפח as well is not needed. The question is worded as a question, but it works as a challenge to רב כהנא's practice.

keyTerms.meaning: He found him
Does the master not hold?: a polite challenge to a scholar's view
It is permitted / kosher

phrases.english: Rav Ashi found Rav Kahana
making an expansive handbreadth,
and making the form of a doorway.
He said to him:
Does the master not hold that ruling of Rava,
as Rava said:
And it is also permitted with the form of a doorway?
phrases.notes: The lenient version (step 10).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the disagreement between the two versions of רבא through a real case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's practice of making both a טפח שוחק and a צורת הפתח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a צורת הפתח alone is enough (lenient version of רבא), then building the טפח too is unnecessary.

steps.title: רב כהנא follows the stricter version of רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that he follows the other version of רבא, which requires the צורת הפתח in addition to the טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like the other version of רבא, where רבא said: And it also needs a doorway-frame.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends his practice. He is not doing extra work; he follows a different version of רבא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed only the lenient version. רב כהנא answers that he holds the strict version from step 11, where both the טפח and the צורת הפתח are required. So doing both is necessary for him, not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The other version (of a teacher's words)
I hold / that is my opinion

steps.whatToRemember: There are three versions of רבא on the corner-shaped סוכה. In the first, only a צורת הפתח works. In the second, the צורת הפתח is just another option besides the טפח. In the third, the צורת הפתח is required together with the טפח. רב כהנא followed the third version in practice.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I, like the other version of Rava,
hold.
As Rava said:
And it also requires the form of a doorway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא כְּאִידַּךְ לִישָּׁנָא דְּרָבָא סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge by pointing to the strict version of רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the ruling (אידך לישנא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא holds that a צורת הפתח alone is enough, so building the טפח too is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the strict version of רבא, both are required, so רב כהנא's practice is correct.

steps.title: רבא: a valid סוכה wall also counts as a wall for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא 'שתים כהלכתן'. רבא adds that this kind of wall also counts as a wall for שבת, because of the reasoning of מגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: two walls built properly, and so on. רבא said: The same is true for שבת. Since it counts as a wall for סוכה, it counts as a wall for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא about two proper walls plus a טפח and opens a new topic. רבא says this setup also works as a wall for the laws of carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a wall for שבת needs to be more complete than a טפח. רבא uses מגו ('since'): because the תורה treats it as a real wall for סוכה, it also gets the status of a wall for שבת, so the סוכה area becomes a private domain. Sefaria explains that this only applies on a שבת during סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their law: built in the proper, full way
Since: because it has a status in one area, it gets that status in another
Wall / partition
With regard to (a specific area of law)

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the laws of סוכה with the laws of carrying on שבת. It raises the question of whether a lenient rule in one area can carry over into another.

phrases.english: "Two in their proper manner, etc."
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא: two full walls and a third of a טפח.

phrases.english: Rava said: And likewise for Shabbat,
since it is a wall with regard to sukka,
it is a wall with regard to Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתַּיִם כְּהִלְכָתָן כּוּ׳. אָמַר רָבָא: וְכֵן לְשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: whether the סוכה wall also counts for שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because two walls plus a טפח count as walls for סוכה, they also count as walls for שבת (מגו).

steps.title: אביי challenges the מגו from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether we really say מגו here. He quotes a ברייתא that says a סוכה wall is like a שבת wall, as long as there is no gap of three טפחים between reeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: Do we really say 'since'? But a ברייתא teaches: A סוכה wall is like a שבת wall, as long as there are not three טפחים between one reed and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins an objection to רבא's rule. He brings a ברייתא that compares סוכה walls and שבת walls. The ברייתא continues in the next step, and אביי draws out his challenge in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא let the סוכה rules set the standard for שבת. This opening part of the ברייתא only says that both kinds of wall share the rule about gaps of less than three טפחים. The real force of אביי's challenge comes from the ברייתא's continuation in step 16, and he states his inference in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from an earlier source)
But a ברייתא teaches
Provided that / only if
Reed / stick

steps.confusionAlert: The 'less than three טפחים' rule here is the idea of לבוד: small gaps count as closed. It is not a new kind of wall, just how reed walls are built.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
And do we say "since"?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
The wall of a sukka is like the wall of Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּין קָנֶה לַחֲבֵרוֹ
phrases.english: provided that there will not be between one reed and its fellow
three handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's מגו rule from step 14 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of מגו to make a סוכה wall count for שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the שבת wall as the model for the סוכה wall, which seems to go against letting סוכה leniencies create a שבת wall. The full argument continues next.

steps.title: The ברייתא's ending: שבת walls are stricter than סוכה walls
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that אביי quoted continues. For שבת, a wall works only if its standing parts are more than its open parts. A סוכה wall does not need this.
steps.simpleTranslation: But שבת is stricter than סוכה. For שבת, carrying is allowed only when the standing part of the wall is more than the open part. This is not so for a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that אביי started in the last step. This ending is the part אביי will use against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the ברייתא said a סוכה wall is like a שבת wall when there are no gaps of three טפחים. Now it adds one difference: for שבת, the wall also needs more standing than open. A סוכה with two walls and a small third wall of one טפח is still kosher, even though most of it is open.

keyTerms.meaning: Stricter; goes further than
The standing part of the wall is more than the open part
Is permitted (here: carrying is allowed)
The open, breached part of a wall

phrases.english: But Shabbat is stricter than sukkah,
for on Shabbat carrying is not permitted
except where the standing part is more than the open part,
phrases.notes: The solid sections of the wall must add up to more than the gaps.

phrases.english: which is not so with a sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that אביי began quoting in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That a סוכה wall does not automatically count as a שבת wall, which would mean there is no מגו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting the wall rules for שבת and סוכה.

steps.title: אביי: so we do not say the 'since' reasoning
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the ברייתא as saying that even on שבת during סוכות, the שבת rule stays stricter. That would mean we do not say מגו, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the ברייתא not saying that שבת during סוכות is stricter than the סוכה itself? Then we do not say מגו!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי spells out his challenge. He says the ברייתא shows that a סוכה wall does not become a שבת wall, even during סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that since a wall counts for the סוכה, it also counts for שבת. אביי says the ברייתא holds the opposite: during סוכות itself, the wall can be kosher for the סוכה and still fail for שבת. If so, the ברייתא rejects רבא's מגו.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not the case that...? (opens a forced reading of a source)
The שבת that falls during סוכות
We do not say

phrases.english: What, is it not
that Shabbat during Sukkot is stricter than the sukkah,
and so we do not say 'since'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in steps 15-16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement in step 14 that a סוכה wall also counts for שבת because of מגו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא is about שבת during סוכות and still requires more standing than open, then the סוכה wall did not become a שבת wall. That means no מגו.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא compares an ordinary שבת to שבת of סוכות
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers by rereading the ברייתא: the comparison is between a regular שבת during the year and a שבת during סוכות. On a שבת during סוכות, מגו does apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא means that an ordinary שבת is stricter than a שבת during סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by reading the ברייתא differently. It is not comparing סוכה to שבת during the same week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On an ordinary שבת, a wall must have more standing than open. On a שבת during סוכות, a סוכה-style wall works for שבת too, because of מגו. So the ברייתא supports רבא instead of disproving him.

keyTerms.meaning: In general; ordinary (here: an ordinary שבת during the year)
No (opens a rejection of the proposed reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings say 'שבת is stricter.' The whole argument is about what שבת is being compared to: the סוכה (אביי's reading), or a שבת during סוכות (רבא's reading).

phrases.english: No:
ordinary Shabbat is stricter
than Shabbat during Sukkot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source (changing what is being compared)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא compares the סוכה to שבת during סוכות, so מגו does not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא compares an ordinary שבת to a שבת during סוכות. During סוכות, the סוכה wall works for שבת because of מגו.

steps.title: If so, the ברייתא should also teach where a סוכה on שבת is easier
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back on רבא's reading. If the ברייתא is talking about שבת during סוכות, it should also teach the reverse case. An ordinary סוכה needs a טפח שוחק, but a סוכה on שבת should be fine with just a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the ברייתא also teach that an ordinary סוכה is stricter than a סוכה on שבת. An ordinary סוכה needs a טפח שוחק, but a סוכה on שבת does not need a טפח שוחק, and a לחי is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's new reading. He asks why the ברייתא lists only one direction and leaves out the matching case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If walls 'cross over' during סוכות, it should work both ways. A לחי is enough for a שבת alley, so on שבת a לחי should also be enough as the third wall of a סוכה shaped like an alley. Since the ברייתא never mentions this, אביי argues it was not talking about שבת during סוכות at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge built on the previous answer)
Let it also teach
A slightly wide טפח, needed for the small third wall of a סוכה
A side post of any width, used to allow carrying in an alley on שבת
And it is enough

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up how far רבא's מגו really goes. Does it only make a סוכה wall count for שבת, or does it also let a שבת-style wall count for the סוכה?

phrases.english: If so, let it also teach:
an ordinary sukkah is stricter than a sukkah on Shabbat,
for an ordinary sukkah
requires a slightly wide handbreadth,
while a sukkah on Shabbat
does not require a slightly wide handbreadth,
and a side post is enough.
phrases.notes: A לחי is the side post used for an alley on שבת. It can be any width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 18, that the ברייתא compares an ordinary שבת to a שבת during סוכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא were discussing how rules cross over during סוכות, it should also list the reverse leniency (a לחי is enough for a סוכה on שבת). Since it does not, the reading seems wrong.

steps.title: אביי Backs Up His Challenge With רבא's Own Ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves that the reverse case is real and worth teaching. He points out that רבא himself ruled that a סכך placed over a מבוי with a לחי makes a valid סוכה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, you yourself are the one who said: If someone put סכך over a מבוי that has a לחי, the סוכה is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is finishing his challenge from Step 19. He shows that the 'reverse case' he asked about is not made up. It is רבא's own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19, אביי argued that if the ברייתא were talking about שבת during סוכות, it should also teach that a סוכה on שבת can rely on just a לחי. Here he proves this rule exists, because רבא himself said it. So the question gets sharper: why would the ברייתא leave out a rule that רבא holds?

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway with houses opening onto it, closed on three sides
A thin side-post at the open end of a מבוי, which lets people carry there on שבת
He put on the roofing (סכך)
Valid, fit to use

phrases.english: For after all, you are the one who said:
phrases.notes: אביי quotes רבא's own ruling back at him

phrases.english: If one placed roofing over an alleyway
phrases.notes: He uses the walls of the מבוי as the walls of his סוכה

phrases.english: that has a side-post, it is valid!
phrases.notes: Valid on שבת because of מגו: since the לחי counts as a wall for שבת, it counts for סוכה too

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the evidence behind the challenge in Step 19
steps.raayaObject: That the reverse מגו case (a סוכה relying on a לחי on שבת) is a real rule the ברייתא should have taught
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's own ruling: סכך over a מבוי with a לחי is valid
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of the ברייתא as talking about שבת during סוכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבא holds the reverse rule, the ברייתא should have mentioned it. Since it did not, maybe the ברייתא is not talking about שבת during סוכות at all.

steps.title: רבא: The Reverse Case Is Too Obvious to Teach
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא did not need to teach the reverse case. If we borrow a rule from the lighter מצוה‎ (סוכה) for the stricter one (שבת), we can surely borrow from the stricter one for the lighter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: That case did not need to be said. Now that we say a rule carries over from the lighter מצוה to the stricter one, then from the stricter מצוה to the lighter one, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his reading. The ברייתא left out the reverse case because it is obvious, not because it is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already teaches the 'harder' direction. A סוכה-style wall works for שבת during סוכות, even though שבת is a very severe prohibition. Once that is true, a שבת-style wall (a לחי) working for a סוכה, which is a lighter מצוה, follows by כל שכן. So the ברייתא's silence does not disprove רבא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not needed, so there was no reason to say it
The lighter one. Here it means סוכה, a positive מצוה
The stricter one. Here it means שבת, a severe prohibition
All the more so, so it is obvious

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'lighter' and 'stricter' describe how serious each מצוה is: סוכה is a positive מצוה, while breaking שבת is a very severe sin. They do NOT describe which wall rule is easier to meet.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's מגו works in both directions. The ברייתא only taught the harder direction (from סוכה to שבת), because the other direction (from שבת to סוכה) follows by כל שכן.

phrases.english: That one was not necessary to state,
phrases.notes: רבא is speaking: the ברייתא had no need to teach the reverse case

phrases.english: now, if from the lenient to the stringent we say it,
phrases.notes: From סוכה (lighter) to שבת (stricter), which is what the ברייתא teaches

phrases.english: from the stringent to the lenient, is it not all the more so?
phrases.notes: From שבת to סוכה is obvious, so it did not need to be written

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Steps 19-20
steps.terutzResolutionType: The missing case is obvious (a כל שכן), so the ברייתא had no need to state it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the ברייתא does not mention a סוכה relying on a לחי on שבת, it must not be talking about שבת during סוכות, and so it rejects מגו
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches only the harder direction (from סוכה to שבת). The easier direction (from שבת to סוכה) follows by כל שכן. So רבא's reading and his מגו both stand.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common way the גמרא reads a source: a text may leave out a case because it is obvious, not because it disagrees with it.

steps.title: Returning to רבא's Ruling Itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new section with גופא. It goes back to study רבא's ruling about סכך over a מבוי on its own terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself. רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is leaving the אביי-רבא debate and preparing to quote רבא's ruling in full so it can study it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling was only brought up in passing as part of the argument. The word גופא signals that the גמרא now wants to look at that ruling directly. רבא's actual statement comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': going back to study a statement that was earlier quoted only in passing

phrases.english: The matter itself. Rava said:
phrases.notes: Sets up a fresh look at רבא's ruling about סכך over a מבוי; the ruling itself continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ruling quoted in Step 20 to study it on its own
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רבא's ruling (stated on the next amud) about placing סכך over a מבוי that has a לחי
